section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section raises a difficulty with the preceding concept.
This section notes that we find nations of the world transgressing the Seven Noachide Laws they were commanded.
section.t: Behold, we find nations of the world transgressing the Seven Noachide Laws that they were commanded.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the simple resolution, drawing on the parallel with the Jewish people, that either a spirit of folly or the heart's dominance over the mind causes the transgression, contrary to their essential nature.
section.t: in the manner explained regarding the Jewish people,
because of a spirit of folly that enters him and covers and conceals the truth, which contradicts that which is called Eloka d'Elokaya.
But from their own perspective, as they are influenced from the kelipos and sitra achra, they are in a manner that they will not transgress and will not rebel,
and like Bilaam who said, "I cannot transgress the word of Hashem"
even though he came upon his donkey
which is from the Seven Noachide Laws.
"Because of the greatness and intensity of their iniquity" their heart rules over their mind
(in the manner explained regarding the Jewish people – Tanya ch. 17),
even though this is the opposite of the natural outcome also in a Noachide
